**Reading map:** Deisenroth, Faisal & Ong, *Mathematics for Machine Learning* (2020), §3.5. This is an original lesson using our delivery-operations example—not reproduced textbook content.

## Why the concept matters

A basis of unit-length, mutually perpendicular directions makes coordinates easy to read. PCA later uses orthonormal principal directions to avoid redundant feature coordinates.

## Define the mathematical relationship

$$
\boldsymbol q_i^\top\boldsymbol q_j=\delta_{ij},\qquad Q^\top Q=I
$$

The displayed relationship is the main object to analyse. Specify the relevant dimensions, quantities and assumptions before using it. It should be read as a mathematical statement, not merely a programming shorthand.

## Work through an original example

The vectors q1=(1,0) and q2=(0,1) form an orthonormal basis of R^2. If x=(3,4), then x=(q1^T x)q1+(q2^T x)q2=3q1+4q2.

## What follows, and what does not

Orthonormality is stronger than independence. Columns of a rectangular matrix can be orthonormal without spanning the entire ambient space.

## Test your reasoning

Normalise (3,4) and verify that its Euclidean norm is one.
